title: Perseverance in Faith
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Perseverance in faith means continuing to trust, follow, and remain faithful to Christ through trials, weakness, opposition, temptation, and time. God keeps His people, and His people continue with Him.
summary: Perseverance in faith means continuing to trust, follow, and remain faithful to Christ through trials, weakness, opposition, temptation, and time. God keeps His people, and His people continue with Him.
christFocus: Jesus Christ preserves His people and will bring them safely to the end. Believers persevere because the risen Lord intercedes, strengthens, and keeps those who belong to Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Christian life requires continuing faith. Scripture warns against shrinking back and calls believers to hold fast, endure, and remain grounded in the hope of the Gospel.

Perseverance is not self-salvation. God is the One who keeps His people, yet He keeps them through faith, warning, encouragement, discipline, prayer, and the means of grace.

Perseverance may happen through weakness and tears. It is not always dramatic victory. Sometimes it looks like returning to Christ again, refusing to quit, and holding on to His promises in the dark.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers fear their weakness or repeated battles mean they cannot finish. Others assume a past profession means they need not continue in faith.

This doctrine gives both comfort and warning. Christ keeps His people, and His people are called to keep looking to Him until the end.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Keep building yourself up in faith and looking to Christ. Do not throw away your confidence when hardship comes. Use Scripture, prayer, fellowship, repentance, and worship as God’s means of strengthening you to endure.
